applied.problem: "Divide the largest reading" works only for an axis from zero (the freezer's largest is −10 °C) and "next step up" skips an exact fit; the examples are not measured; "appropriate curve" also covers a straight line; dot-to-dot line graphs of records are normal.

The rule of thumb forbids dot to dot for all measured points, wider than the explanation now allows: records with no steady pattern, such as weekly sales, are commonly drawn as dot-to-dot line graphs.

The laid line is judged by a fixed rule (within half a square, some on each side), not by eye, and no later lesson in this course works a best-fit line out exactly, so "come later" is untrue for that part.
On the freezer screen the time axis runs along zero, partway up the graph with readings below it, so "time along the bottom" is untrue there.

notes.problem: Every reading is a value chosen for the example (ignores and the caption call them example values), so each number's kind should be "assumed", or "computed" for the fitted-line figures, not "constant".
Line B (least squares of 19, 15, 12, 10, 6, 3 cm) ends at 18.619 − 0.7786 × 20 = 3.05 cm, so its label's "3.1 cm" should read "about 3 cm"; the screen itself shows no figure.
